Algorithm-agnostic Besag-Clifford selective Hotelling test (arbitrary clustering)

Source: R/besag_clifford.R
selective_hotelling_bc.Rd

A Monte Carlo selective test of equality of the means of a discovered cluster pair (k1, k2), valid after clustering X with an arbitrary black-box clustering routine cl_fun, treating the covariance \(\Sigma\) as unknown. It is the package's entry point for selective inference after any clustering algorithm (hierarchical clustering, fixed-init k-means, spectral clustering, ...), in contrast to selective_hotelling_test(), which is hard-wired to k-means.

The construction is exactly that of Besag and Clifford (1991), transported to the Stiefel manifold. Under the null the observed polar factor \(Q_{obs}\) is uniform on the feasible region \(E = \{Q \in St(r-1, p) : cl\_fun(X(Q))\ \mathrm{preserves}\ (k_1,k_2)\}\) regardless of \(\Sigma\). We build a Metropolis kernel \(K\) on \(E\) using a symmetric Cayley proposal \(Q' = U Q\) (with \(U\) a random Cayley rotation of step eps) that is accepted iff \(Q' \in E\); for a flat target restricted to \(E\) this acceptance ratio is the indicator \(1\{Q' \in E\}\), so \(K\) (and \(K^L\)) is reversible w.r.t. \(\mathrm{Uniform}(E)\). We then plant \(Q_{obs}\) at a uniform random index \(J \in \{0,\dots,M\}\) and run \(K^L\) forward \(J \to M\) and backward \(J \to 0\). Because the seed is stationary and \(K^L\) reversible, the rank of the contrast statistic \(u(Q) = \|Q'v\|^2\) (which is strictly monotone in the pair's two-sample Hotelling \(T^2\)) of \(Q_{obs}\) among the \(M+1\) path marks is exactly \(\mathrm{Uniform}\{1,\dots,M+1\}\). Hence the randomized upper-tail rank p-value is exactly \(\mathrm{Uniform}(0,1)\) under \(H_0\).

Validity holds for ANY reversible kernel, ANY step eps, ANY path length M, and ANY clustering cl_fun. Mixing (governed by eps, L, and the acceptance rate) buys power only, never validity.

Usage

selective_hotelling_bc(
  X,
  cl_fun,
  k1,
  k2,
  M = 5000L,
  L = 2L,
  eps = "mixture",
  randomized = TRUE,
  eps_range = c(0.001, 1),
  cl_obs = NULL,
  ridge = 1e-08,
  stiefel_tol = 1e-08,
  guard_feas_checks = 25L,
  oracle_Sigma = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  kernel = c("givens", "cayley", "givens_slice"),
  slice_max_props = 200L
)

Arguments

X

A numeric \(n \times p\) data matrix with observations in rows.

cl_fun

A black-box clustering routine: a function function(Xmat) -> integer label vector (or a list carrying $cluster, e.g. the result of stats::kmeans()). It must be a pure function of its data argument (only data-independent randomness is allowed, e.g. a fixed initialization or a deterministic algorithm such as hierarchical clustering). It is called once on X to obtain the observed clustering and many times on reconstructed data \(X(Q)\) during sampling.

k1, k2

The two tested cluster labels, in the labelling of cl_fun(X). Each cluster must have at least three members for a Hotelling \(T^2\).

M

Path length; the path carries M + 1 marks. Validity holds for any M >= 1; larger M reduces Monte Carlo error.

L

Number of kernel steps per path edge (i.e. \(K^L\)). Larger L improves spread/mixing and hence power.

eps

"mixture" (default) draws a step size independently for each path edge from the fixed log-uniform eps_range. A positive numeric value uses a fixed step size, and NULL uses 0.3. The step size is never tuned on the observed point, because that can break exactness.

randomized

If TRUE (default) returns the randomized upper-tail rank p-value, which is exactly \(\mathrm{Uniform}(0,1)\) under \(H_0\); if FALSE, ties are broken conservatively.

eps_range

Bounds of the fixed log-uniform step-size mixture.

cl_obs

Optional precomputed cl_fun(X) (saves one call); otherwise it is computed internally.

ridge

Small non-negative ridge added to the pooled covariance when computing the reported observed \(T^2\) via hotelling_T2().

stiefel_tol

Guard tolerance on \(\max|Q'Q - I|\) over the path (GUARD a).

guard_feas_checks

Number of path points to re-verify with the generic feasibility predicate (GUARD b).

oracle_Sigma

Optional known \(p \times p\) covariance matrix. If supplied, an additional known-\(\Sigma\) oracle p-value is computed on the same path by ranking the Mahalanobis statistic \(d' \Sigma^{-1} d\) of the pair-mean difference; returned as p_oracle. Validity is identical; only the statistic (hence power) differs.

verbose

If TRUE, print a one-block diagnostic.

kernel

Proposal of the Metropolis kernel. "givens" (default; the random Givens kernel of the paper) picks two rows \(i < j\) of \(Q\) uniformly at random and proposes \(Q' = G_{ij}(\omega) Q\), a rotation by angle \(\omega \sim N(0, (\pi\,\mathrm{eps})^2)\) in that coordinate plane (see givens_left()). Both proposals are symmetric and preserve the uniform law on the Stiefel manifold, so both kernels are reversible w.r.t. \(\mathrm{Uniform}(E)\) and the p-value is exact for either; they differ only in mixing, hence power. "cayley" proposes \(Q' = UQ\) with \(U\) a random Cayley rotation of step eps, which moves every row of \(Q\) at once. eps, eps_range and the "mixture" rule apply to both. "givens_slice" is the shrinking-bracket Givens move (the shrinkage step of elliptical slice sampling; Neal 2003; Murray, Adams and MacKay 2010): it picks rows \(i < j\) uniformly, draws \(\omega_0 \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0, 2\pi)\), sets the bracket \([\omega_0 - 2\pi, \omega_0]\) (which contains the current point \(\omega = 0\)), proposes \(\omega = \omega_0\) and, while the proposal is infeasible, shrinks the bracket toward 0 and redraws \(\omega\) uniformly in it. It is reversible w.r.t. \(\mathrm{Uniform}(E)\), needs no step size (eps and eps_range are ignored) and nearly always moves, at the price of several cl_fun calls per step (see n_path_calls).

slice_max_props

For kernel = "givens_slice": maximum number of proposals (calls of cl_fun) in one shrinking-bracket step; if all fail the chain stays put. The cap is symmetric in the two directions of a move, so the kernel stays reversible and the p-value exact.

Value

An S3 object of class "selectiveHotelling": a list whose primary fields are pval (the randomized Besag-Clifford p-value), se (its Monte Carlo standard error), T_obs (the observed two-sample Hotelling \(T^2\) of the tested pair), draws (the vector of path statistic values used for ranking), acc (kernel move fraction), n_unique_draws, k1, k2, K (number of distinct labels in the observed clustering), condition_on ("pair-preserved"), and sampler ("besag-clifford"). Additional diagnostic fields are also returned: p_cons (conservative tie-broken p-value), p_oracle, M, L, eps, u_obs, path_u, J, move_frac, stiefel_max, feas_ok, n_feasible_path, kernel, n_path_calls (calls of cl_fun made by the kernel along the path, the compute measure for comparing kernels) and n_cluster_calls (all calls of cl_fun made by this function, including the observed clustering when cl_obs is not supplied, step-size calibration and the guards).

See also

selective_hotelling_test(), hotelling_T2()

Examples

set.seed(1)
X <- matrix(rnorm(30 * 2), 30, 2)
# A deterministic, data-pure clustering routine (hierarchical clustering).
hclust_cl <- function(Xmat) {
  hc <- stats::hclust(stats::dist(Xmat), method = "average")
  as.integer(stats::cutree(hc, k = 3))
}
cl <- hclust_cl(X)
# Pick a pair with at least 3 members each.
sizes <- table(cl)
big <- as.integer(names(sizes)[sizes >= 3])
res <- selective_hotelling_bc(X, hclust_cl, big[1], big[2], M = 60)
res$pval
#> [1] 0.6985158
print(res)
#> Selective Hotelling T^2 test (unknown covariance)
#>   Clusters tested : 2 vs 3 (of K = 3)
#>   Sampler         : besag-clifford
#>   Conditioning    : pair-preserved
#>   Observed T^2    : 38.05
#>   Selective p-val : 0.6985 (MC s.e. ~ 0.059)
